analysis.title: The Next AI Squeeze JPM Reveals Who Could Be Forced To Buy
key_insights: After a large positioning reset in the AI trade, JPM sees a possible second wave of buying into year-end. Hedge funds are underexposed, QQQ short interest is at its highest since 2023, and leveraged exposure has been cut sharply.
Retail is buying the dip. JPM puts equity ETF purchases at $20bn per day last week and $30bn on Monday.
Leveraged equity ETFs took in nearly $5bn over Nov 5-6, equal to roughly $15bn of leveraged exposure. Inverse ETFs saw about $5bn of outflows over the past week.

By Nov 5, leveraged equity ETF exposure relative to underlying market cap had unwound nearly 90% of the increase built between April and June. The rebound in leveraged ETF buying starts from a much smaller base.

QQQ short interest is at its highest level since 2023 and Nasdaq futures positioning has been heavily reduced. The caveat is that not all QQQ shorts are directional, since some hedge existing long exposure, which limits squeeze fuel.

Retail options activity has been reset. Small-lot call buying is well below its early-June peak, and retail's share of options trading is close to its one-year low per JPM's Retail Radar. Cash-equity buying has returned but options buyers have not, which leaves a further source of upside demand.

The momentum long/short factor is down about 40% from its peak, its largest unwind since the post-GFC recovery. October's 11% fall in the long momentum-versus-market portfolio was roughly a six-sigma event, and shorter-term crowding measures are near historical extremes.
Retail net bought about $1.6bn of NVDA over Nov 5-11, the most purchased stock of the week. Buying intensity reached 3.7 standard deviations on Monday and 4.7 on Tuesday.

Retail buying is narrow. Mag 7 purchases ran at +1.1 standard deviations over the past week while technology stocks outside the group were sold at -1.1. Semiconductors kept getting bought, while hardware and software were sold.

JPM's sequence: continued retail support stabilizes AI stocks through November, then hedge funds rebuild positions from late November onward, a second wave of demand. The risk is that retail runs out of buying power before institutions return.
